lesson_title: Two Pizza Places, One Lying Average
hook_text: Both flyers say 'average delivery: 40 minutes'. One is telling the truth. One is hiding chaos. The math that exposes it:
clip_script: Two pizza places both print the same promise on the flyer: average delivery, 40 minutes. Place one runs a tight kitchen: deliveries take 38, 39, 40, 41 or 42 minutes. Place two sends one scooter across the whole suburb: deliveries take 25, 30, 40, 50 or 55 minutes. Both average exactly 40 — yet nobody would call them the same service. The quickest wandering-meter is the range: slowest delivery minus fastest. Place one: 42 minus 38, a range of 4 minutes. Place two: 55 minus 25, a range of 30. One number each, and the flyer's trick is exposed. An average reports the CENTRE of the data; it says nothing about how far the data WANDERS.
visual_style: Split screen of two delivery scooters: one arriving in a tight metronome rhythm, the other swinging wildly early and late, with delivery times stamping onto two number lines that squeeze into a short box and a stretched box.
pacing: Matching flyers side by side, quick delivery montage, freeze on the two ranges 4 vs 30, snap to the box plots for the visual verdict.
